scope: One owned Ubuntu 22.04 aarch64 VM, kernel 6.8.0-138-generic. Different struct files only. Same-file distinct-acquirer races and exec_reconcile remain open. Not an x86 result.

control.barrier: Child-process /dev/fuse daemon holds the first FUSE_FLUSH of the victim node. The loser thread blocks inside do_dup2. The winner dup3 completes, including its fexit, before that flush is released.
opcode_order: FLUSH node 3 answered while unique 16 was still held (unique 18)

diagnostics.meaning: The winner do_dup2 fentry reads the kernel fdtable after the loser has installed its file and before the loser fexit publishes. That mismatch increments state_errors. The race oracle does not require history_gaps to be false. Serial alias coverage still requires it.

not_claimed: Same struct file acquired by two pidfd_getfd callers. File-pointer equality is true for both fexits, so a delayed fexit can still overwrite the winner acquirer.
exec_reconcile still deletes a slot when an unlocked real_slot read disagrees during do_close_on_exec.
x86 and other kernels were not run.
Clearing state_errors to make this race look gap-free.
